MANUAL CHECKS (15) — automation cannot judge these
  · Test with a real screen reader (NVDA or JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS/iOS).
    why: No automated tool, and no simulator, reproduces real AT behaviour — NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver diverge from each other and from the specification.
  · SC 2.4.3: Tab through the page and confirm the focus order is logical, not merely present.
    why: a11y-loop can see that focus moves and where it goes, but whether the sequence makes sense for this content is a human judgment.
  · SC 2.1.1: Complete the page’s main task using only the keyboard.
    why: Automated checks probe individual controls; they do not know what the user is trying to accomplish.
  · SC 1.1.1: Confirm the alt text on 7 images is accurate and useful, and that decorative images use alt="" rather than a description.
    why: Automation can only see whether alt text exists. alt="decorative image" passes every automated rule and is worse than alt="". If any alt text was generated by an AI, treat it as a draft that a human must confirm.
  · SC 3.3.3: Submit the form with 8 fields in an invalid state and confirm each error is announced, identifies the field, and says how to fix it.
    why: SC 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 are about whether an error message is actionable, which no tool can assess. Error states also usually only exist after interaction — audit them with --interact.
  · SC 2.4.6: Confirm every field label describes what to enter, not just that a label exists.
    why: A label of "Field 1" satisfies every automated rule and tells the user nothing.
  · SC 2.4.4: Read each link text out of context and confirm the destination is still clear.
    why: SC 2.4.4 permits vague link text when the surrounding context supplies the purpose — whether it does is a judgment call.
  · SC 1.3.1: Confirm the heading structure describes the content hierarchy, not the visual sizes.
    why: Automation can detect skipped levels but not whether the outline reflects the actual structure of the page.
  · SC 1.4.10: Confirm the table still conveys its meaning at a 320px viewport.
    why: SC 1.4.10 excepts content requiring two-dimensional layout. Whether a given table qualifies, and whether it remains understandable, needs a person.
  · SC 4.1.2: Review the 30 ARIA attributes on this page: is each one appropriate, or merely valid?
    why: Pages using ARIA average more accessibility errors than pages without it (WebAIM Million 2026: 59.1 vs 42.0). A role is a promise — role="button" commits to the full keyboard behaviour of a button. No ARIA is better than bad ARIA.
  · SC 2.1.2: Confirm each dialog announces itself on open and describes how to dismiss it.
    why: a11y-loop tests the focus trap, Escape, and focus return mechanically. Whether the dialog is comprehensible when announced is a screen-reader test.
  · SC 2.3.3: Confirm any animation that survives prefers-reduced-motion is genuinely essential.
    why: The "essential" exception cannot be evaluated automatically.
  · SC 1.4.1: Confirm colour is never the only way information is conveyed.
    why: SC 1.4.1 is one of the criteria no tool can test: recognising that "the required fields are in red" needs comprehension of the content.
  · SC 1.4.3: Check the contrast of the elements axe could not measure by hand (WebAIM Contrast Checker, or a11y-loop contrast <fg> <bg>).
    why: axe gives up on background images, gradients, pseudo-element backgrounds and foreground opacity or occlusion, and reports them as incomplete. A computed ratio of 1:1 is the usual tell.
  · SC 1.4.11: Check the contrast of hover and focus states.
    why: No engine checks state contrast unless the state is driven and re-scanned. Use --interact to add hover and focus states to the audit.
